chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, raising it, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding
a man who ate from the flesh of a hunted prey not knowing what it was, and he was in Ihraam. He said: 'Upon him is blood of a sheep'.

key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: one in the state of Ihraam (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What is the compensation for eating game meat while in Ihraam?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the fidya (compensation) for a muhrim who unknowingly consumes game meat, prescribing the slaughter of a sheep. This ruling highlights the principle of ease in Shia jurisprudence, distinguishing between intentional and unintentional violations of Ihraam restrictions. The specific mention of 'sheep' rather than a broader category of livestock underscores the precise application of sacrificial duties in Hajj rituals.
